name: Lightweight Structures: Cellular, Sandwich & Architected Materials
summary: Shows how to make structures as light as possible by combining material choice with shape: foams, honeycombs, sandwich panels, lattices and hybrid materials.

topics.name: Lightweighting strategy: material, shape, and structural efficiency
Cellular solids: honeycombs and foams; Gibson-Ashby scaling laws
Metallic, polymeric and ceramic foams: processing and properties
Sandwich panel design: face and core selection, failure-mode maps
Architected lattice materials: stretching- vs bending-dominated lattices, Maxwell's criterion
Designing hybrid materials: filling holes in property space
Lightweighting case studies: aircraft, vehicles, bicycles and space structures
Lightweight frames for wearable exoskeletons: stiffness, strength and fatigue constraints
